title: Traceability matrix (.qa/trace/matrix.json)
description: What qa trace matrix writes: for every requirement its criteria and test cases, whether it is proven on the target commit, its open findings and its gaps; every test case with the latest result of each automated test on the target commit; and the gaps over the whole chain. Derived from the state alone, so the same state gives the same bytes.

target.description: the full commit every result row was chosen for; results of other commits are never used

target_source.description: present when the command chose the target: given with --target, or head, the working tree's commit

tree_dirty.description: present with target_source head: whether the working tree differed from that commit when the matrix was made. Results are judged by the executions' own dirty flags, shown on each test row

counts.description: gaps per kind, every kind present

proven.description: it has criteria, and each has a test case whose oracle is not characterization and whose tests all passed on the target

status.description: failed if any test failed (flaky counts as failed), else blocked or inconclusive, else not_run when a test has no passing result, else passed; null when no test has a result on the target

red_check.description: an execution in which one of its tests failed an assertion is linked

commit.description: the commit of the result row (the target), null when the test has no result on it

dirty.description: the execution's own git fact: it ran on a tree that differed from the commit; null when the test has no result on the target

diff_hash.description: present only when dirty: the execution's diff hash
